summary: EU, UK, US and Indian passport holders, among others, need Azerbaijan's ASAN e-Visa: a single-entry visa for a 30-day stay, issued online within 3 working days (USD 20 state fee plus a USD 9 service fee). Citizens of Türkiye, Russia, Ukraine, Georgia, Belarus, Moldova, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, the Gulf states, China, Japan and South Korea enter visa-free under bilateral agreements or temporary unilateral waivers.

notes: The UK government's travel advice says you need an export certificate to take antiques or art — such as carpets, samovars, copperware or paintings — out of Azerbaijan; the vendor or the Azerbaijan National Carpet Museum can provide one.

Canada's travel advice says some prescription medicines may not be available and that you are responsible for checking whether yours are legal in Azerbaijan; keep them in the original container with a copy of the prescription.

tips.text: The UK government's travel advice says anyone who has visited certain areas in south-western Azerbaijan, including the town of Khankendi, without the Azerbaijani authorities' permission could be denied entry, and advises contacting an Azerbaijani embassy or consulate before you travel. The border with Armenia is closed.

Canada's travel advice says all land border crossings have been closed since 2020, except for freight, and that Canadian passport holders can only enter by air. The UK government says entry by land or sea is restricted and that you need the authorities' permission to leave by road.

The UK government's travel advice says that if you stay longer than 15 days you must register with the State Migration Service, online or in person, and that if you do not you will have to pay a fine before you can leave. Hotels often do this for their guests; otherwise you must do it yourself.
Azerbaijan's official electronic visa portal is ASAN Visa, at evisa.gov.az.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Azerbaijan?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do. Citizens of many countries, including the EU, UK, US and India, apply online for the ASAN e-Visa (USD 29 in all, issued within 3 working days, 30-day stay). Türkiye, Russia, Ukraine, Georgia, Belarus, Moldova, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Serbia, Albania, Morocco, the Maldives, the Gulf states, China, Hong Kong, Macao, Japan, South Korea, Singapore and Bosnia and Herzegovina are visa-free, and the remaining nationalities apply for a visa at an Azerbaijani embassy or consulate.

faq.question: How fast is the ASAN e-Visa?
faq.answer: The standard e-Visa is issued within 3 working days, and the urgent e-Visa within 3 hours, regardless of holidays and non-working days. The portal asks you to apply at least 3 working days before your planned arrival. The e-Visa is for a single entry and a stay of up to 30 days.

faq.question: Can I enter Azerbaijan if I have been to Armenia?
faq.answer: The UK government's travel advice says anyone who has visited certain areas in south-western Azerbaijan, including the town of Khankendi, without the Azerbaijani authorities' permission could be denied entry, and advises contacting an Azerbaijani embassy or consulate before you travel. No official source we could read says how a visit to Armenia itself is treated at the border.

faq.question: Can I cross into Azerbaijan by land?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says all land border crossings have been closed since 2020 except for freight, and that Canadian passport holders can only enter by air. The UK government says the land borders with Georgia and Iran are temporarily closed.

faq.question: Do I need to register my stay in Azerbaijan?
faq.answer: Yes, if you stay more than 15 days. The UK government's travel advice says you must register with the State Migration Service, online or in person, and that if you do not you will have to pay a fine before you can leave. Hotels often register their guests; otherwise you must do it yourself.
